definitions.explanation: Grass or other plants that have been cut and dried for use as animal feed or bedding. A fundamental agricultural product used especially for feeding horses, cattle, and other livestock.

examples.japanese: {馬|うま}に{干|ほ}し{草|くさ}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: I give hay to the horses.

examples.japanese: {納屋|なや}には{干|ほ}し{草|くさ}がたくさん{積|つ}んであった。
examples.english: Lots of hay was stacked up in the barn.

examples.japanese: {牧場|ぼくじょう}では{夏|なつ}の{間|あいだ}に{干|ほ}し{草|くさ}を{作|つく}って{冬|ふゆ}に{備|そな}える。
examples.english: At the ranch, they make hay during summer to prepare for winter.

notes:
Composed of {干|ほ}す (to dry) + {草|くさ} (grass). Written as {干し草|ほしくさ} or {干草|ほしくさ}. The round bales of hay seen in pastoral landscapes are called {干|ほ}し{草|くさ}ロール or {牧草|ぼくそう}ロール.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}し{草|くさ}を{刈|か}る: to cut hay
- {干|ほ}し{草|くさ}の{山|やま}: haystack
- {干|ほ}し{草|くさ}の{匂|にお}い: the smell of hay
- {干|ほ}し{草|くさ}アレルギー: hay allergy

RELATED WORDS:
- {牧草|ぼくそう}: pasture grass, fodder — fresh or dried grass for livestock
- {藁|わら}: straw — dried stalks of grain crops like rice, distinct from hay
- {飼料|しりょう}: animal feed — the general term for all livestock feed
